\section{Weighted Laplacian and Rayleigh quotient}
\label{sec:laplacian}
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite connected graph with symmetric positive edge
weights $w_{xy} = w_{yx} > 0$ for $\{x,y\} \in E$. For each vertex $x \in V$,
let $d_x = \sum_{y \sim x} w_{xy}$ be its weighted degree, and for any subset
$S \subseteq V$ define its volume $\operatorname{vol}(S) = \sum_{x \in S} d_x$
and boundary weight $w(\partial S) = \sum_{x \in S,\, y \notin S} w_{xy}$.
The normalized Rayleigh quotient of a nonzero function $f : V \to \mathbb{R}$
is given by
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:rayleigh-quot}
\mathcal{R}(f) = \frac{\sum_{\{x,y\} \in E} w_{xy} (f(x) - f(y))^2}{\sum_{x \in V} d_x f(x)^2}.
\end{equation}
Let $0 = \lambda_1 < \lambda_2 \le \dots \le \lambda_{|V|}$ denote the
eigenvalues of the normalized weighted Laplacian on $G$, and let
$h(G) = \min_{0 < \operatorname{vol}(S) \le \operatorname{vol}(V)/2}
\frac{w(\partial S)}{\operatorname{vol}(S)}$ be the weighted Cheeger constant.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:rayleigh}
The first nontrivial eigenvalue $\lambda_2$ admits the variational
characterization
\[
\lambda_2 = \min \left\{ \mathcal{R}(f) : f \not\equiv 0,\ \sum_{x \in V} d_x f(x) = 0 \right\},
\]
where $\mathcal{R}(f)$ is defined in \eqref{eq:rayleigh-quot}.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Since the constant functions span the kernel of the normalized weighted
Laplacian and are orthogonal to the subspace $\{f : \sum_{x \in V} d_x f(x) = 0\}$
in the degree-weighted inner product, the Courant--Fischer min-max principle
gives the stated formula.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:spectral-lower}
For every finite connected weighted graph $G$, the spectral gap satisfies
$\lambda_2 \ge \frac{1}{2} h(G)^2$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Let $f$ be a minimizer realizing $\lambda_2$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:rayleigh},
shifted by a median so that its positive part $g = f_+$ is supported on a set
of volume at most $\operatorname{vol}(V)/2$ and satisfies $\mathcal{R}(g) \le \lambda_2$.
Applying the co-area formula to the level sets of $g^2$ and bounding the edge
variation by Cauchy--Schwarz produces $h(G) \le \sqrt{2 \mathcal{R}(g)} \le \sqrt{2\lambda_2}$,
and squaring gives $\lambda_2 \ge \frac{1}{2} h(G)^2$.
\end{proof}

\section{Cut bounds and counter collisions}
\label{sec:cuts}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:cut-upper}
For every nonempty proper subset $S \subset V$,
\[
\lambda_2 \le \frac{w(\partial S)}{\operatorname{vol}(S)} + \frac{w(\partial S)}{\operatorname{vol}(V \setminus S)}.
\]
\end{proposition}

% Intentionally decrement counter to simulate a duplicate printed number anomaly.
\addtocounter{proposition}{-1}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:cut-refined}
For every subset $S \subset V$ with $0 < \operatorname{vol}(S) \le \operatorname{vol}(V)/2$,
\[
\lambda_2 \le 2 \frac{w(\partial S)}{\operatorname{vol}(S)}.
\]
\end{proposition}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:cheeger}
For every finite connected weighted graph $G$,
\[
\frac{1}{2} h(G)^2 \le \lambda_2 \le 2 h(G).
\]
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Choose $S \subset V$ achieving $h(G)$ with $0 < \operatorname{vol}(S) \le \operatorname{vol}(V)/2$,
and set $f(x) = \operatorname{vol}(V \setminus S)$ for $x \in S$ and
$f(x) = -\operatorname{vol}(S)$ for $x \notin S$.
Applying Lemma 1 to the indicator test vector $f$ gives
$\lambda_2 \le \mathcal{R}(f) = w(\partial S)\bigl(\operatorname{vol}(S)^{-1} + \operatorname{vol}(V \setminus S)^{-1}\bigr) \le 2 h(G)$.
Combining this with Theorem 1 yields $\frac{1}{2} h(G)^2 \le \lambda_2 \le 2 h(G)$.
\end{proof}

The constant in Proposition 2.1 can be sharpened for regular graphs.

\begin{claim*}
If $G$ is connected with $h(G) > 0$, then by Theorem~\ref{thm:spectral-lower}
the spectral gap $\lambda_2$ is strictly positive.
\end{claim*}

\appendix

\section{Auxiliary discrete bound}
\label{sec:app-bound}
\setcounter{lemma}{0}
\renewcommand{\thelemma}{A.\arabic{lemma}}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:app-sum}
For every function $g : V \to \mathbb{R}$,
\[
\sum_{\{x,y\} \in E} w_{xy} |g(x)^2 - g(y)^2|
\le \sqrt{2 \sum_{\{x,y\} \in E} w_{xy} (g(x) - g(y))^2}
    \sqrt{\sum_{x \in V} d_x g(x)^2}.
\]
\end{lemma}
